finding.text: `ext/Chat/Composer.js:82` turns `on_error` from a visible note into `console.warn` only, trusting the new always-visible `$diag` line to carry every error instead — but several of `Dictate.js`'s own `set_error()` calls never call `log_step()` first, so `$diag` never updates for them. The worst case is `Dictate.js:374-376` (`start()`'s very first check, `insecure_context_message()`) — exactly the owner's own setup for this ticket, dictating over plain `http://10.0.0.135:3104` from a phone. With this change, that error now shows nowhere: not in `$diag` (no `log_step` call), not in `$note`/placeholder (on_error no longer writes there), and the full text is parked inside `$info`, which `Composer.js:142-163` moves bodily into the hidden full-screen gear menu. The owner gets a silent failure instead of the "wasting lines on an old error" problem they actually complained about. `Dictate.js:651` (Whisper stopped answering mid-segment) and `:748` (Chrome's 6-second silent-failure watchdog) have the same gap. Fix: add a `log_step("mic", …)` (or a new stage) right before each of these three `set_error()` calls, same pattern already used for the watchdog and `browser_error()` in this diff.

`Mic.js`'s revived `watch_capture()` (around line 139) re-arms by calling `this.watch_capture()` again on the fresh capture — correct, but worth a quick headless check that a second `track.ended` firing immediately after a revival (flaky hardware, not just a pause) doesn't race past the `this.reviving` guard, since `reviving` is cleared in a `finally` right after the awaited `fresh.start()`, not after `watch_capture()` has finished re-arming.

`Composer.js`'s `note()` revert now also resets `$note.text(hint)` after 4s (good — this is the actual fix for "old artifact error" lingering), but it is a timer, not a true "stage recovered" signal; a slow 5s round-trip send could have its "nothing was sent" note silently replaced by `hint` a second before the real result would have written over it anyway. Harmless today since nothing currently takes longer than the 4s window, but worth naming as a timer, not a recovery check, in case a future caller's `deliver()` is slower.
